subject: maths
pattern: Area under curves is a regular 5-mark (and 3-mark) item: area of ellipse/circle, area between a parabola and a line, or area bounded by two curves, along with one or two 1/2-mark direct integrals. Draw the rough sketch, shade the region, find the points of intersection, set up limits, integrate and state the answer in square units.

questions.q: Write the formula for the area bounded by the curve $y=f(x)$, the x-axis and the ordinates $x=a$, $x=b$.
Write the area of the circle $x^2+y^2=a^2$.
Find the area under $y=x^2$ between $x=1$ and $x=2$.
Find the area under the curve $y=\sin x$ between $x=0$ and $x=\pi$.
Find the area under $y=\sqrt{x}$ from $x=0$ to $x=4$.
Find the area of the region bounded by the curves $y=x^2$ and $y=x$.
questions.answer: Intersection: $x^2=x\Rightarrow x=0,1$. In $[0,1]$ the line is above the parabola. Area $=\int_0^1(x-x^2)dx=\left[\frac{x^2}{2}-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^1=\frac12-\frac13=\frac16$ square unit.

questions.q: Find the area of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$.
questions.answer: The ellipse is symmetric about both axes, so Area $=4\times$ (first-quadrant area). In the first quadrant $y=\frac ba\sqrt{a^2-x^2}$. Area $=\frac{4b}{a}\int_0^a\sqrt{a^2-x^2}\,dx=\frac{4b}{a}\left[\frac x2\sqrt{a^2-x^2}+\frac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1}\frac xa\right]_0^a=\frac{4b}{a}\cdot\frac{a^2}{2}\cdot\frac{\pi}{2}=\pi ab$ square units.

questions.q: Find the area of the region bounded by the parabola $y^2=4x$ and the line $x=3$.
questions.answer: The region is symmetric about the x-axis. Area $=2\int_0^3 y\,dx=2\int_0^3 2\sqrt x\,dx=4\left[\frac23x^{3/2}\right]_0^3=\frac83\cdot3\sqrt3=8\sqrt3$ square units.

questions.q: Using integration, find the area of the triangle with vertices $(1,0)$, $(2,2)$, $(3,1)$.
questions.answer: Sides: $AB: y=2(x-1)$, $BC: y=4-x$, $AC: y=\frac{x-1}{2}$. Area $=\int_1^2\left[2(x-1)-\frac{x-1}{2}\right]dx+\int_2^3\left[(4-x)-\frac{x-1}{2}\right]dx$. First: $\frac32\cdot\frac12=\frac34$. Second: $\int_2^3\left(\frac92-\frac{3x}{2}\right)dx=\frac92-\frac32\cdot\frac52=\frac34$. Area $=\frac34+\frac34=\frac32$ square units.

questions.q: Find the area enclosed between the curve $y=\cos x$ and the x-axis from $x=0$ to $x=2\pi$.
questions.answer: Since $\cos x$ changes sign, split the interval: Area $=\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos x\,dx+\left|\int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}\cos x\,dx\right|+\int_{3\pi/2}^{2\pi}\cos x\,dx=1+2+1=4$ square units.

questions.q: Find the area of the region bounded by the parabola $y^2=4ax$ and its latus rectum.
questions.answer: Latus rectum is $x=a$. The region is symmetric about the x-axis. Area $=2\int_0^a y\,dx=2\int_0^a 2\sqrt a\sqrt x\,dx=4\sqrt a\left[\frac23x^{3/2}\right]_0^a=\frac{8a^2}{3}$ square units. [Sketch: parabola opening to the right with vertex at origin; shaded region between curve and the line $x=a$.]

questions.q: Find the area of the region enclosed between the circle $x^2+y^2=16$ and the parabola $y^2=6x$.
questions.answer: Solving: $x^2+6x-16=0\Rightarrow x=2$ (points $(2,\pm2\sqrt3)$). Area $=2\left[\int_0^2\sqrt6\sqrt x\,dx+\int_2^4\sqrt{16-x^2}\,dx\right]$. First: $\sqrt6\cdot\frac23\cdot2\sqrt2=\frac{8\sqrt3}{3}$. Second: $\left[\frac x2\sqrt{16-x^2}+8\sin^{-1}\frac x4\right]_2^4=4\pi-2\sqrt3-\frac{4\pi}{3}=\frac{8\pi}{3}-2\sqrt3$. Area $=2\left[\frac{2\sqrt3}{3}+\frac{8\pi}{3}\right]=\frac43(4\pi+\sqrt3)$ square units.
